To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the production of B cell stimulator factor-2 (BCSF-2) and interferon gamma (IFN-gamma) was shown in cerebrosplinal fluids collected from mice with viral meningitis and from patients with viral meningitis or encephalitis and that these findings suggest that activated T cells are required to develop disease and produce both BCSF-2 and INF-gamma.

the production of B cell-stimulation factor-2 and IFNgamma was shown in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of patients with acute viral infection of the central nervous systems (CNS) and in a murine infection model.
B cell stimulatory factors are produced in the CNS during viral meningitis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of cytokines in the central nervous systems of patients and mice.
the role of cytokines in the pathogenesis of CNS disease.
the role of cytokines in the pathogenesis of viral meningitis and the development of a model for studying the pathogenesis of this disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BSF-2 is produced by the central nervous system in the context of viral infections and that this production is regulated by T cell activation.

the production of BSF/IL-6 in the CSF of mice with viral encephalitis and of patients with viral CNS infections is a result of a complex and dynamic process of T-cell and B-cell activation and proliferation.
the production of both B cell stimulatory factors (BSF- 2) and IFNs in the CNS is a general feature of viral meningitis and that it may be important for the development of disease.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we showed that both B-cell stimulating factor 2 and IFN gamma are synthesized in CSF of both experimental viral meningitis and in patients with acute viral CNS infections.

the production of B cell stimulator factor 2 (BSF2) and interferon gamma (INFgamma) in the central nervous systems is shown in cerebro-spinal fluids (CSFs) collected from mice and patients with experimental viral meningitises.
the production of B cell stimulating factor-2 (IL-6) and interferon gamma (IFN-gamma) in the central nervous systems of both mice and humans during viral infections of the CNS was evaluated.
The main takeaway from our work is that
both IFN-gamma and BSF-2 are produced by activated T lymphocytes in the CNS during viral meningitis.

both BSF- 2 and IFN- gamma are produced in the central nervous systems (CNS) of mice with experimental viral meningoencephalitis and in patients with viral CNS disease, suggesting an important role of these cytokines in local immunological responses in the CNS.
both B cell stimulatory factors and interferon are synthesized in the CNS in response to viral infection.
